business_problem: Shutterfly needed to move massive photo-content workloads off rigid, expensive relational databases so it could scale billions of assets and seasonal peaks more flexibly and at lower cost.
solution_summary: Shutterfly standardized on MongoDB Atlas on AWS to support the brands that store, edit, and serve billions of customer photos and personalized products. The company recreated its existing multi-dataset topology in Atlas, with clusters up to six terabytes in size, and used Mongomirror to synchronize the legacy environment with Atlas while production applications kept running. That approach let the team cut over a multi-terabyte estate in minutes with minimal downtime. Atlas now handles thousands of transactions per minute, gives Shutterfly a document model that is easier to evolve than its former relational schemas, and lets engineers scale up for seasonal events such as Christmas and Valentine's Day before scaling back down again. The same platform also makes cloning environments and preparing multi-tenant partner services much simpler than in the old datacenter model.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Runs Shutterfly's production document database clusters on AWS for photo, project, and content workloads across multiple brands.

solution_components.name: Mongomirror
solution_components.role: Synchronized the existing database environment with Atlas during migration so applications could keep running until cutover.

data_flow: Customer photos and project data flow into MongoDB Atlas clusters on AWS, Mongomirror kept legacy and Atlas environments synchronized during migration, and the new platform serves editing and ordering workloads across Shutterfly's brands while scaling for peak demand.
business_outcome: Shutterfly reduced infrastructure cost by up to 20%, gained easier seasonal scaling and environment cloning, and created a multi-cloud-ready platform for future partner services without the rigidity of relational databases.
